chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from some of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) — he said:

I said: 'There happens to be a testimony with me for a man from my brethren, and the judges among us do not accept all of it.' He said: 'So when you know that it is true, then correct it by every means until his right is established for him.'

key_terms.الْقُضَاة: judges — here referring to Abbasid-appointed judges whose criteria for admissible testimony may have differed from Imami standards
key_terms.حَقّ: right/truth/due — carries dual meaning: the testimony is 'haqq' (true), and the man's 'haqq' (entitlement) must be vindicated
key_terms.شَهَادَة: testimony/witness — a formal legal term in Islamic jurisprudence referring to eyewitness evidence given before a court
key_terms.فَصَحِّحْهَا: correct/authenticate it — imperative form, directing the narrator to validate the testimony by all available legitimate means

ai.seo_question: What should a believer do if he knows a testimony is true but judges will not accept it?
ai.summary: A narrator poses a practical legal question to Imam al-Sadiq (AS): he holds testimony that would vindicate a fellow believer's right, but the local judges (operating under Abbasid rule) would not accept all of it. The Imam's response establishes an important jurisprudential principle: if one has personal certainty of the truth of a claim, one must use every permissible means to ensure the rightful claimant receives his due. This reflects the Imami approach to navigating unjust judicial systems while upholding substantive justice — the believer is not absolved by procedural obstacles from the moral duty to help his brother obtain what is rightfully his.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Usman Bin Isa, from one of his companions, 
(The narrator) says, Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said,

‘I said, ‘There happened to be for the man from my brethren, a testimony with me, and the judges among us did not allow all of it’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘So when you know that it is true, so correct it with each aspect of it, to achieve his right for him’.
en.sarwar: 3. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from ‘Uthman ibn ‘Isa from certain persons of his people who has narrated the following: “I once said to abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, that I bear a testimony for one of our brothers but all of the judges around us do not grant it.
He (the Imam) said, ‘If you know that it is right then you can correct it as such that can prove his right.’”
